status: D05-frozen; hypothesis-specific raw-scale margins and final seed allocations remain D07 inputs
evidenceBoundary: Outcome-blind design validation only; no experiment outcomes were generated or analyzed.

e03Amendment.reason: Full bounded simulation showed the former five-percent high-seed cap was not a calibrated test and reduced complete-rule power below 0.10 in every registered variance row.
e03Amendment.independentUnit: seed/run success proportion over 200 repeated episodes
e03Amendment.controlEquivalence: Five TOST p-values for bounds [0.20, 0.30], Holm-adjusted at family-wise alpha 0.05.
e03Amendment.oracleAdequacy: One-sided seed-level t test and 95% lower bound above 0.90.
e03Amendment.oracleSeparation: Five paired seed-level oracle-minus-control t tests above 0.60, Holm-adjusted at family-wise alpha 0.05; report conservative 99% Bonferroni lower bounds.
e03Amendment.bootstrapRole: Seed bootstrap intervals are sensitivity estimates, not primary gates, because the smallest-row percentile interval undercovered in independent simulation.
e03Amendment.highSeedRule: Every non-oracle seed at or above 0.35 triggers case-level leakage review; no arbitrary count is itself a statistical rejection.
e03Amendment.invalidRuns: Use the next ordered reserve only for a prespecified validity failure; report all attempts; fewer than N valid runs yields incomplete primary analysis; additionally report invalid-as-failure sensitivity without converting it into the primary estimate.

validationAcceptance.monteCarloInterval: two-sided 95% Wilson interval on simulation success count

confirmedFindings: Production normal, Student-t, one-sample and Welch tests, TOST, Holm, Wilson, exact-binomial, type-7 quantile, log-beta, entropy, mutual-information, and beta-binomial-fit values agree with independent R references.
Wilson and seed-level t intervals attained at least 0.94 lower Monte Carlo coverage bounds in the registered stress cases.
The 999-resample percentile bootstrap at N=25 had 0.9335 estimated coverage with upper 95% Monte Carlo bound below 0.95, so it is sensitivity-only.
TOST boundary false-equivalence estimates ranged from 0.0071 to 0.0109 at nominal per-test alpha 0.01.
Ignoring seed clusters inflated the stress-case Type I estimate to 0.3081; seed-level inference estimated 0.0406.
All four bounded full-E03 numeric-rule rows exceeded the 0.90 lower Monte Carlo power floor after removing the uncalibrated high-tail count rejection.
Treating five percent of N=75 runs as failures drove numeric-rule power to zero in the registered stress case; this is a deliberately severe sensitivity, not a replacement for reserve accounting.

confirmatoryFamily.procedure: One valid p-value per member, global Holm at family-wise alpha 0.05; composite members contribute the maximum component p-value and require all practical directions.
confirmatoryFamily.selectionRule: D07 must transform each frozen raw-scale practical margin and pilot variance into a member-specific standardized effect, simulate that member's complete test including composites and missingness, then choose the largest required primary-seed count whose lower 95% Monte Carlo power bound is at least 0.90. The ten-seed publication floor and historical 75-seed convention are not power justifications.
